ai.description: *Ichthyophis beddomei* reaches 30 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a pale venter. It features 250–300 annular grooves and a terminal shield. Family: Ichthyophiidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis beddomei* is distinguished by a distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that runs along its body, unlike the broken or absent stripes of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis beddomei* inhabits moist, shaded soil near streams within tropical evergreen forests and plantations, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nilgherries caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis beddomei* is oviparous, laying 20–30 eggs in terrestrial burrows guarded by the female. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis beddomei* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily found in the states of Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nilgherries Caecilian emits a series of soft, high-pitched, rhythmic clicks or chirps, typically heard from within damp soil or leaf litter near forest streams.
